target_customer: Freight forwarders, logistics providers, parcel carriers, retailers and manufacturers that need item level shipment and inventory tracking
problem: Shipments and inventory are hard to track affordably at item level; traditional trackers cost over 100 dollars per unit and RFID needs readers and infrastructure.
business_model: Hardware label sales (a cellular label retails for about 25 dollars per unit per founder quotes) plus a tracking platform
product_category: Printed active wireless smart labels for supply chain tracking

founders.name: David Stanton
founders.background_notes: Named co-founder and chief executive by SiliconANGLE (Nov 2025) and YC page; he said the company fell into the idea by accident while discussing an airline logistics pain point.

founders.name: Brian Krejcarek
founders.background_notes: SiliconANGLE says he had spent years experimenting with ultra low cost disposable circuits that became foundational to the labels. Crunchbase title differs from SiliconANGLE.

competitors.name: Roambee
competitors.what: IoT tracker combining Bluetooth, Wi-Fi and GSM for real time cargo monitoring
competitors.funding_then: Series B of about 4.1 million dollars in January 2017, with a 2018 investment from MDI Ventures per search summary

technical_complexity.rationale: Making thin, flexible, active wireless labels at very low cost needs novel disposable circuits, printed electronics and later cellular and Bluetooth integration; the company says it was the first to reach mass production of such labels.

defensibility.rationale: Manufacturing know how in printed active labels is hard to replicate, but large label and tracking players such as Avery Dennison and Zebra are adjacent.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: SiliconANGLE in 2025 lists Avery Dennison, Zebra and Tag-N-Trac as rivals; none acquired Reelables in sources found.

market_need_then: Supply chain visibility needs were large and existing trackers were costly; Roambee had raised venture funding for tracking in 2017 and 2018, showing demand for monitored shipments, but no Reelables specific 2019 demand data was found.

branding.domain_note: Uses reelables.com (exact name .com); acquisition history not found.
branding.brand_signature: Trademarked Track Anywhere smart label product name

brand_strength.rationale: Trade press covers product launches, but the name is easily misspelled as Realables in some coverage and no brand assets or community were found.

outcome_analysis: Reelables spent years developing mass producible printed active labels, launching a Bluetooth label in 2019 and a cellular label in 2023, then raised a 10.4 million dollar Series A in November 2025 with revenue growth reported at 200 percent that year. The deep manufacturing and hardware problem slowed funding relative to software companies, and the company is still active and scaling production toward 100 million labels a year.
notes: Series A of 10.4M on 2025-11-17 is stated by SiliconANGLE and by FreightWaves, Built In and MMH headlines; investor list from SiliconANGLE (Seedtable lists PJC Ventures as lead, which company coverage does not). The GlobeNewswire release returned 403 and was not opened. An aggregator (startupintros) lists a 1M seed in April 2019 with angel Peter Sonsini and CB Insights reports 11.55M total over 6 rounds; both are aggregator only and unverified, so there is a gap between the recorded round and the total. Founding year 2018 from trade coverage summaries. Competitors named by SiliconANGLE in 2025 (Avery Dennison, Zebra, Tag-N-Trac) are not used as founding era competitors; Tag-N-Trac was founded in 2020. Roambee dated source is January 2017; its 2018 MDI investment comes from a search summary. The outcome search returned no results about Reelables.
